# atoom, vendored

[atoom](https://github.com/truvity/atoom) holds the ports, drivers and kits that sluis shares with session and ritueel. sluis's own contracts import atoom's messages (`proto/sluis/store` imports `atoom/common/v1alpha1/common.proto`), and sluis hosts the drivers of its key port (`atoom/key/v1alpha1`) of its item port (`atoom/store/v1alpha1`) of its source port (`atoom/source/v1alpha1`) and of its four audit ports (`atoom/blob/v1alpha1`, `atoom/transport/v1alpha1`, `atoom/index/v1alpha1`, `atoom/destination/v1alpha1`), so the proto files of atoom are copied here, unchanged, at the commit named in [PIN](PIN). Nothing here is edited by hand.

- `proto/`: the proto files of every atoom port, from `<port>/proto/atoom/` at the pinned commit. `buf` reads them as a dependency; they are not an output (`buf.gen.yaml` leaves them out), because the generated Go comes from atoom's own modules, `github.com/truvity/atoom/<port>`, which `go.mod` requires. The Go package of each file is set in `buf.gen.yaml` (managed mode) to that module's `gen` directory.
- `versions.yaml`: atoom's pinned runtimes at that commit. `just atoom-check` holds this repository's ConnectRPC, Protobuf and buffa pins to it, as the plan says: atoom bumps first, then the consumers.
- `PIN`: the source, the commit, and the sha256 of the files above.

The Rust side takes the crates of atoom that sluis uses as git dependencies at the same commit (`[workspace.dependencies]` of the root `Cargo.toml`): `atoom-common` (the refusal helpers) and, for the item port, `atoom-store-rqlite` (the rqlite driver's library, which `drivers/store/rqlite` hosts), `atoom-store-memory` and `atoom-store-conformance` (the in-memory engine and the suite, in store@'s tests and in the host's `conformance` command), `atoom-socket` (the client the suite dials with) and `atoom-store` (the contract, for the tests that call a driver directly). For the source port it takes `atoom-source-file` (the file driver's library, which `drivers/store/file` hosts and `store check --validate` reads a directory with) and `atoom-source-credential` (the credential driver's library, which `drivers/store/credential` hosts), and `atoom-source` (the contract, for the tests that call a driver directly). For the audit ports it takes `atoom-blob-fs` (the fs blob driver's library, which `drivers/writer/fs` hosts), `atoom-blob-fsreadonly` and `atoom-blob-fsdir` (the read-only driver and the directory code both share, which `drivers/indexer/fs` hosts), `atoom-transport-spool` (the spool, which `drivers/writer/spool` hosts), `atoom-index-sqlite` (the sqlite index driver, which `drivers/indexer/sqlite` hosts, and the tests of the indexer and the reader), `atoom-destination-dir` (the directory driver, which `drivers/exporter/dir` hosts), `atoom-destination-conformance` (the `Destination` trait, its service, the in-memory driver and the suite, which exporter@ and its tests use) and the contracts `atoom-blob`, `atoom-transport`, `atoom-index` and `atoom-destination` (for the tests that call a driver directly). The conformance kits of these ports (`blob-conformance`, `transport-conformance`, `index-conformance`, `destination-conformance`) are binaries of atoom that run against a driver's socket in any language; the hosts' `conformance` commands run the backend suite of atoom's library. `sluis-proto` also generates the vendored messages (`connectrpc-build` cannot point a message at another crate), so it holds a second, wire-identical copy of `Refusal`, `IndexEntry`, the item, source, blob, transport, index and destination messages, which store@, the audit actors and exporter@ speak through; the helpers of the refusal detail come from `atoom-common`.

To move to another commit: `just atoom-sync <commit>` (40 hex digits; needs the network), then `just proto-gen`, and commit everything. `just atoom-check` (in `just check-rules`, offline) fails when the commit differs between `go.mod`, `Cargo.toml` and the PIN, or a vendored file changed. Until atoom has a release the pin is a commit; the first release (`v0.1.0`) replaces the commit by the tag in all four places.

- `testdata/slotplan-vectors.json`: the vectors of the slot map check of `github.com/truvity/atoom/key/slotplan`, which the Rust twin of that check (`actors/store/src/config/slotplan.rs`) reads, so that both implementations are held to one file. It is part of the PIN's digest.
- **Placeholder versions.** atoom's Go modules require each other at `v0.0.0` until its first release, and a version that has no tag cannot be looked up, so `go.mod` has one `replace` line for each, `<module> v0.0.0 => <module> <the pseudo-version of the pinned commit>`. `just atoom-sync` writes them and `just atoom-check` holds them to the commit; they go away with the move to the tag.
